Because of the scale of the program, broad scope of activities, and the length of time covered, this report was created by combining the individual budget period/annual reports, with a synopsis inserted between each section to elucidate the changes in focus and direction as they evolved over time. In each section, the membership status, education activities, and research and development projects that were carried out are described, along with key metrics. The statement of project objectives (SOPO) is provided as an appendix to this report. The SOPO is the contractual document that details the high-level objectives for each budget period as well as each project to be carried out, with milestones, deliverables, and timelines. This report documents how PowerAmerica achieved its highest objectives; to create a robust U.S. wide bandgap semiconductor ecosystem and to train the workforce needed to support this important manufacturing sector. PowerAmerica was first formed with 24 founding members and grew to 90 members in year nine. Over 3,500 students and working professionals were trained on wide bandgap technology over that timeframe. Through the efforts of the Institute and its members, X-FAB in TX became the world’s first commercial scale silicon carbide foundry. Start-ups as well as established semiconductor companies in the US and around the world have since produced SiC devices at X-FAB. PowerAmerica also helped companies such as GE, John Deere, and Infineon to significantly de-risk new product development with wide bandgap semiconductor technology. PowerAmerica represents a model of successful public-private collaboration to address a critical strategic national objective. 2 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The U.S. Department of Energy’s Advanced Manufacturing Office (predecessor to AMMTO) established PowerAmerica in December 2014 to develop and accelerate the adoption of wide bandgap (WBG) semiconductor chips and power electronics in manufacturing. The objective was to spark early commercialization of energy- efficient products; educate and train the workforce; create high-tech jobs; and nurture the growth of the U.S. WBG semiconductor manufacturing industry. PowerAmerica is led by North Carolina State University by way of a five-year, $140M cooperative agreement with DoE.
